newsitem.title: USA: U.S. needs to open foreign markets to meat - USMEF.
newsitem.headline: U.S. needs to open foreign markets to meat - USMEF.

text.p: The U.S. government should do more to promote freer trade and open foreign markets to U.S. meat despite increases in beef and pork exports in the past few years, a U.S. Meat Export Federation (USMEF) official said on Tuesday.

"My opinion of the current situation in Washington is we give a lot of lip service to freer trade, but we actually are going the other way and I don't like that," said Bryant Wadsworth, USMEF executive vice president of international programmes.

Speaking at the American Farm Bureau Federation Convention here, Wadsworth did not specify what measures the United States should take, but said greater efforts are needed to open markets in China, the Philippines and other countries to U.S. red meats.
"We would like the Israelis to open their market to beef," he said. "They basically closed us out and there is no justification for it."
Exports of U.S. beef and pork in 1997 should exceed 1996 levels and the quantity of 1996 exports was up six percent from the previous year, he said.
"We are doing great, but we are going to do a lot better," said Wadsworth.

In the past 10 years, U.S. beef exports tripled in quantity and increased eight-fold on a value basis, while pork exports quadrupled in quantity and increased eight-fold on a value basis in that time, he said.
The U.S. Agriculture Department is working to upgrade its meat export reports and issue them more frequently using information voluntarily supplied by U.S. meat packing companies.
Wadsworth said the meat packers probably will initially be opposed to the reports, but should soon rely on them as others will.
"My gut feeling is...it will be more timely and in a few weeks (after they are under way) everyone will be addicted to the numbers," he said.
